title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
key_facts: AWS introduced two open-source projects: Strands Decider 2B, a small decision model, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution.

Strands Decider 2B has two billion parameters, is based on Qwen3.5-2B and selects between predefined options with confidence scores, for tasks such as model routing, tool selection, classification and guardrails.
AWS released the weights, training data and scripts; median decision latency is about 115 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 and 153 ms on an Apple M3 MacBook for small tasks.
AWS reports 72.3% accuracy on JevBench across 231 public tasks for its v19 checkpoint.
Strands Box (developer preview) combines operating-system isolation with Dogwood, an open-source policy language that defines which actions an agent can take, based on content and execution history.
InfoQ says the published results do not establish a direct performance advantage over TypeSafe AI's Jev, which is available through a managed API.
GitHub discussions have raised concurrent requests, Apple Silicon compatibility and cold-start latency.
quote_evidence: AWS has introduced two open-source projects for AI agent development: Strands Decider 2B, a small model designed to make decisions within agent workflows, and Strands Box, a sandbox for controlling agent execution.
AWS evaluated Strands Decider using JevBench, although the published results do not establish a direct performance advantage over Jev.
why_it_matters_hint: Controls that sit outside the language model give developers a firmer way to limit what an AI agent can do, though the tools are new and self-reported.
notes: Release date not given; benchmark figures are AWS's own.
